open_points.subject: A17 rule 1 command-line configuration path validation
open_points.text: “The kernel reads the file's path, an absolute one or the kernel refuses to start, from its one command-line argument — with none or more than one it refuses to start too” and later “a path that names no component, empty or `/` alone”
open_points.question: In what order are argument count, absolute-path, no-component, component-open, final-file metadata and file-read checks performed, especially since an empty path is both non-absolute and named as a no-component path?
options: Check argument count, then absolute path, then components and file
Check path form before argument-count errors where possible
Treat all such failures as one undifferentiated startup refusal
open_points.default_guess: Check argument count first, then absolute path, then require a component, then open and validate the file.

open_points.subject: A17 rule 1 startup checks
open_points.text: “the kernel refuses to start” for the new argument-count and absolute-path failures
open_points.question: Where do these new A17 startup checks fall relative to the startup checks in A03, A16, A18 and A20 when more than one would fail, and which failure is reported?
options: Run all A17 invocation and configuration checks before store and sandbox checks
Run store and sandbox checks before A17 configuration checks
Collect and report multiple startup failures
Define another single global startup-check order
open_points.default_guess: Validate the command-line argument and securely read and validate the configuration before opening the store, probing the sandbox or performing recovery.

open_points.subject: A17 rule 1 final-component opening
open_points.text: “the last component for reading with `O_NONBLOCK` as well, so a component that is no regular file is refused by the checks rather than waited on”
open_points.question: What behavior is required for a non-regular final component whose Linux open operation can still block or have device-specific behavior despite `O_NONBLOCK`, since the file cannot be checked as regular until after it has been opened?
options: Use the stated read open and accept that Linux may still block before the regular-file check
Use a separate metadata-only open before opening for reading
Restrict supported filesystems and file types further so the no-wait claim is guaranteed
Drop the guarantee that rejection occurs without waiting
open_points.default_guess: Use `O_RDONLY|O_NOFOLLOW|O_NONBLOCK`, immediately check the opened descriptor, and reject non-regular files, while accepting Linux's actual blocking semantics.

open_points.subject: A17 rule 1 opened path descriptors
open_points.text: “each directory on the way opened with `O_PATH` and `O_DIRECTORY`” and “No descriptor so opened is inherited by a process the kernel starts”
open_points.question: When are the root, intermediate-directory and final-file descriptors closed, and must every configuration read and credential resolution perform a fresh component walk rather than retaining or caching any of them?
options: Fresh walk each time; close each prior directory after opening the next and close the final file after reading
Keep the directory chain open for the duration of the kernel process but prevent inheritance
Keep the final configuration descriptor open and reread that object
Allow implementations to choose any lifecycle that prevents child inheritance
open_points.default_guess: Perform a fresh walk for every read, close intermediate descriptors as soon as they are no longer needed, and close the final descriptor after the checked read.
